name: Momentum Fund - The Impact Band With Real Quotes

momentumSections.body: Behind every event, chapter, and member of our network is a conversation, an introduction, or a shared experience that helped someone move forward. These are a few of them, in the words of the people they happened to.
momentumSections.title: One connection can change what's possible.

testimonials.name: Jessica Li
testimonials.quote: The Harvard in Tech SF event was an incredible opportunity for SF Harvard alums to gather, learn from engineering leaders in different fields, and build connections with operators, founders, and investors. Founders and engineering leaders of top companies came to recruit talent, and it was a great venue for that connection. The Harvard in Tech community is brilliant and very engaged. We're looking forward to the next event and further building out the group here.

testimonials.affiliation: Harvard Extension School Alumni · Class of 2023
testimonials.name: Mohammed Ally
testimonials.quote: Colorado did not have a chapter. We started with six people in a co-working space on a Saturday afternoon. What the fund pays for is the part nobody sees — the space, the coffee, the follow-up that turns a one-time afternoon into something people plan their month around.

description:
The impact band on the real page once quotes exist — the counterpart to the public-visitor scenario, where the collection is still empty and the band renders nothing at all. It shows the two states a quote card has side by side: the first carries a real San Francisco event photo, and the second deliberately carries NEITHER a portrait nor an event photo, so its quote runs the full width of the card. That second state is the point — there is no photo on file for that member, and the event photo he used to have was a generic New York stage shot captioned as a Colorado event it was not from. The card renders honestly without either rather than borrowing a face and a place that are not his.

The frame is scrolled to the band with a hover interaction. It used to rely on seeding the band into first position instead, and that stopped working: the hero is now rendered unconditionally at the top, so ordering can no longer lift anything above it and the capture was silently showing the hero — indistinguishable from every other /donate scenario.
